title: Microsoft Purview: DLP and auto-labeling policies for non-Microsoft connected apps
summary: The briefing's rollout dates, licensing and metering statements, policy limitations and control routes are supported. It correctly highlights the conflicting Microsoft cut-over instructions and the retirement before general availability. A minor correction should acknowledge Microsoft's alternative connector navigation.

claims.claim: Purview is extending DLP and Information Protection auto-labeling to non-Microsoft connected apps.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention and Information Protection Auto-labeling capabilities now extend to non-Microsoft connected apps

claims.claim: The roadmap says supported conditions and actions vary by application.
claims.quote: The conditions and actions supported for each of these applications vary.

claims.claim: The capabilities use Defender for Cloud Apps connectors to reach supported applications.

claims.claim: Automation specifically addressing the new dedicated DLP app locations is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: New-DlpCompliancePolicy dedicated non-Microsoft connected apps Box Google Workspace location parameters API; "non-Microsoft connected" "PowerShell" DLP auto-labeling. Read feature and cmdlet references; ThirdPartyAppDlpLocation is generic, Locations describes Copilot.

claims.claim: The listed Purview auto-labeling route and its note follow the documented wizard through label selection, Full directory and app locations.
claims.quote: Go to Solutions > Information protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies > + Create auto-labeling policy. On What type of auto-labeling policy do you want to create?, choose Automatically apply labels only. Select Custom > Custom policy > Next.

claims.claim: No documented command or API parameter specifically configures auto-labeling for these apps.
claims.quote: Searched: New-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy dedicated non-Microsoft connected apps Box Google Workspace location parameters API. Read feature page and searched full cmdlet reference for Box, Google and location parameters; Locations has no description and no app-specific parameter is named.

claims.quote: In the Microsoft Defender Portal, select Settings. Then choose Cloud Apps. Under Connected Apps, select App Connectors. Select the +Connect an app to add an app and then select an app.
claims.fix: Keep the supported path. Add to controls[2].note: 'Microsoft also documents Cloud Apps > Connected apps > Connect an app (or Add a new connector) at https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-cloud-apps/enable-instant-visibility-protection-and-governance-actions-for-your-apps#enable-app-connectors.' Add that URL to sources.

claims.claim: Defender for Cloud Apps app connector configuration has no documented automation operation.
claims.quote: Searched: "Defender for Cloud Apps" "app connectors" "API" create connector; Defender for Cloud Apps REST API create app connectors file policies automation. Read api-introduction and connector enablement search excerpts; they document portal setup, not an operation to create connectors.

claims.claim: The migration page opens the file-policy list at Defender > Cloud apps > Policies > Policy management > All policies.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft Defender portal, go to Cloud apps > Policies > Policy management. Select the All policies tab.

claims.claim: Defender for Cloud Apps file-policy management has no documented automation operation.
claims.quote: Searched: "Defender for Cloud Apps" "file policies" "REST API" create disable. Read api-introduction, migration page and file-policy search excerpts. These describe portal policy management and provider-API enforcement, not an API to create or disable file policies.

claims.claim: The listed retiring Instances route follows Custom > Custom policy > Admin units > Locations > Instances > Edit > Specific instances > + Include instances.
claims.quote: Open Data loss prevention > Policies > + Create policy. Select Custom > Custom policy. Set the Admin units scope as desired. On the Locations page, toggle the Instances location to on.

claims.claim: New-DlpCompliancePolicy -Name <policy name> -ThirdPartyAppDlpLocation All creates a DLP policy including all connected non-Microsoft cloud apps.
claims.quote: The ThirdPartyAppDlpLocation parameter specifies the non-Microsoft cloud apps to include in the DLP policy. You can use the value All to include all connected apps.

claims.claim: ThirdPartyAppDlpLocation requires Compliance Administrator or Compliance Data Administrator membership.
claims.quote: This parameter requires membership in the Compliance Administrator or Compliance Data Administrator roles in Microsoft Entra ID.

claims.quote:
| Activities | GET or POST | /api/v1/activities/ |

claims.claim: The ThirdPartyAppDlpLocation reference does not identify it as managing the new dedicated application locations.
claims.quote: Searched: New-DlpCompliancePolicy dedicated non-Microsoft connected apps Box Google Workspace location parameters API. Read ThirdPartyAppDlpLocation and Locations and searched the full reference for app names; no passage maps the generic parameter to the new dedicated locations.

claims.claim: Creating replacement Purview policies does not remove original Defender file policies.
claims.quote:
Does migrating remove my original file policies?
No. Migration creates new equivalent policies in Purview.

claims.claim: Activity explorer supports the non-Microsoft connected-app DLP policies.
claims.quote: Activity explorer supports non-Microsoft connected app policies. You can monitor DLP policy activity for your non-Microsoft apps in the same way you monitor Microsoft 365 locations.

claims.claim: Activity explorer supports these auto-labeling policies.
claims.quote: Activity explorer supports non-Microsoft connected app policies. You can monitor labeling policy activity for your non-Microsoft apps in the same way you monitor Microsoft 365 locations.

claims.claim: DLP alerts support these policies.
claims.quote: DLP alerts are supported for non-Microsoft connected app policies. Alerts appear in the DLP alerts dashboard alongside alerts from other locations.

claims.where: Why it matters; controls[3].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: MC1449180 says to turn off or delete overlapping Defender file policies before creating the Purview policy.
claims.quote: Before you create Microsoft Purview policy for any of these non-Microsoft applications, turn off or delete any Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps file policies for the same non-Microsoft locations.

claims.claim: Learn instead says to disable Defender file policies only after validating and turning on Purview policies.
claims.quote: Disable Defender for Cloud Apps policies only after you validate and turn on the Purview policies.

claims.claim: For the new optional policy capability, the sources name no new end-user experience or automatic enforcement for tenants that create no policy.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview non-Microsoft connected apps licensing Enterprise tier Box Google Workspace pay as you go. Read roadmap, MC1449180 and both feature pages: they describe admin-created policies and on/off choices, not automatic new-policy enforcement; the separate retirement is disclosed.
